clue.text: Considered just a trifle

definitions.meaning: considered in the past tense, as in pondered or believed
a very small amount, as in 'add a touch more salt'

explanation.definitionFit: Considered is a past-tense synonym (reflected, judged); the noun also serves idiomatically for a tiny amount, as in 'a shade more sugar'.

clue.text: Set this out for religious people

indicators.note: set out suggests letters laid out afresh, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to lay something out for a group of churchgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal working on SET THIS, whose seven letters rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Believers in a god are religious people, the plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: Striking left a good man to carry on after all others

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
ST, short for saint, is the crossword's usual good man

explanation.surface: A worker on strike leaves a decent fellow to keep going when everyone else has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers 'out' are on strike, so 'Striking' gives OUT rather than suggesting something impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive or endure longer than every rival is the verb's dictionary meaning.

clue.text: A girl's prayer

definitions.meaning: a girl's first name, as Kelly or Rose
a short thanksgiving said before a meal

explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female first name and also the brief blessing spoken at table before eating.

clue.text: Speculates that the love increases

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
something that increases rises

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that affection grows stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is zero in tennis, which gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To form ideas or hypotheses without proof is to speculate.

clue.text: Coarse stuff can be devastating

definitions.meaning: rough cloth such as hessian used to make bags
plundering and laying waste to a captured town

explanation.definitionFit: Hessian bag cloth is rough material, and plundering a city after it falls is laying it waste.

clue.text: Go for "seconds" stuff

parts.note: to stuff is to cram, as a bag or one's mouth

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a second helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'seconds' looks like a second helping but is just the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear off or leave quickly, an imperative command like 'get lost'.

clue.text: Many a politician's agent gets a seat

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many
an MP is a Member of Parliament, so the possessive gives MPS
an agent is a means or instrument, a tool

explanation.surface: A parliamentary candidate's local organiser is rewarded with a constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' tempts as a parliamentary seat; it is a folding stool. 'Many' gives C, the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A light folding stool used outdoors is a kind of portable seat.

clue.text: Exhibiting minimal sense in a bird sanctuary

parts.note: a bird's place of safety and rest is its nest

explanation.surface: A dull-witted person is found at a bird reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sanctuary is a single nest, not a reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word for silly or senseless, so showing the least possible intelligence.

clue.text: Old king — a scoffer, so more influential

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, a monarch of the past
to scoff is to eat greedily, so a scoffer is an eater

explanation.surface: A former monarch was a mocker and thus gained more sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffer' suggests a mocker, but 'scoff' also means wolf down food. GR is King George's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Of larger importance or power, the comparative of an adjective meaning eminent.

clue.text: Dearest form of dais

indicators.note: a different form of the word means its letters are reshaped into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A cherished type of raised platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges the letters of DEAREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform in a room, an uncommon synonym of the platform word in the clue.

clue.text: A mad rush to push buttons

parts.note: to push forcefully is to ram
Buttons is the traditional nickname of a uniformed page boy, from his rows of buttons

explanation.surface: A frantic dash to press the buttons on a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttons' is the old British nickname of a hotel page boy in a brass-buttoned uniform, also the pantomime character in Cinderella.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent frenzied charge about the place is a wild, mad rush.

clue.text: Trapped by strange instrument

parts.note: caught in a trap means snared
rum is an old British word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out by an unfamiliar musical device.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as strange is dated British slang, as in 'a rum business'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drum with wires across its lower skin is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: How to extract metal from fish

definitions.meaning: to melt ore so as to separate out the metal
a small silvery fish related to salmon

explanation.definitionFit: Heating ore to draw out the metal is the refining process, and the word is also a small silvery food fish.

clue.text: Like turning brown, it's the very devil!

indicators.note: turning here means the word for like is read backwards

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Getting a deep suntan is said to be hellishly bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reads the word for like backwards, giving SA; 'brown' tempts as a colour adjective but simply supplies the shade word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief evil spirit in Christian belief is the Devil himself.

clue.text: Homes for retired women, always in order

definitions.text: Homes for retired women, always in order

parts.words: Homes for retired women, always in order
parts.note: reads like care homes for pensioners kept tidy; really the women have retired from the world and belong to religious orders

explanation.surface: Residences for elderly ladies are always kept neat and tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests old age, but here it means withdrawn from the world; 'in order' means members of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Convents house women who have withdrawn from worldly life and belong to a religious order.

clue.text: Advocate taking drink after drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls
porter is a dark brown beer

explanation.surface: A campaigner has one drink after another.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER is a dark beer, once popular with London market porters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who backs or champions a cause is an advocate for it.

clue.text: Possibly stopped round about when put off

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters are placed around the word for about
possibly signals that the letters of the next word may be rearranged into some other order

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in 'a talk on birds'

explanation.surface: Someone may have halted something circling about when it was delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' scrambles the clue's 'stopped' into POSTPED, and 'round' wraps that around the short word for about; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off is to delay or defer something to a later time.

clue.text: Patiently awaited verdict

parts.note: reads as a court ruling waited for calmly; really the verdict a patient waits for from the doctor

explanation.surface: A jury's decision is waited for calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patiently' is read as by the patient: the doctor's verdict on an illness, not a jury's.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's identification of an illness is the medical verdict a sick person waits for.

clue.text: A vessel with another inside is not light

indicators.note: inside means the second vessel goes within the first

parts.note: a dish is a vessel for food
another vessel, Noah's boat, the ark

explanation.surface: A container nested within a second one is quite heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like weight, but it is the opposite of dark. The two vessels are a dish and Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat dark in shade, so lacking brightness.

clue.text: He's shown clearly total cure may be effected

parts.note: to total is to add up

indicators.note: a cure effected in another way means its letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor's evidence shows that complete recovery can be achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be effected' rearranges the letters of 'cure' into UCER. The definition reads as 'he has shown clearly': an adducer is someone who brings forward proof.
explanation.definitionFit: One who adduces cites evidence or examples to show plainly that a claim holds.

clue.text: See copper's place in court matters

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, followed by the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A police officer's role in legal affairs is examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a place, used in law as in locus standi, the right to be heard in court.

clue.text: Everybody is after honour, that's material

indicators.note: after places the words for everybody and is following the honour

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A remark that everyone chases distinction, and that is what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British award, the honour here. 'material' hints at importance but means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A light soft fabric of wool or silk is a dress material.

clue.text: Bearing with a person making advances? Fine!

parts.note: a compass bearing, south, abbreviated S
someone who advances money is a lender

explanation.surface: A man with good manners flirts and is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' suggests romantic overtures but means loans; 'Bearing' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and delicate, as in a fine thread or a narrow margin.

clue.text: Wrinkle free and middle-aged!

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

indicators.note: the middle part of the hyphenated word means only the central letters of aged are taken

explanation.surface: Someone is line-free and in mid-life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-aged' splits: 'middle' takes GE from 'aged'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised crease or fold on a surface, a small line like a wrinkle.

clue.text: Upset a porter — be a baddie

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Knock over a railway porter and turn villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges A PORTER BE.
explanation.definitionFit: An unprincipled scoundrel is a villain, a bad character.

clue.text: Quite proper, though blue

definitions.meaning: conservative in politics, blue being the British Tory colour

explanation.definitionFit: Correct and fitting, and politically conservative, since blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.

clue.text: Game played in a gaming room breaking all rules

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A card game played in a casino defies every regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'room breaking', where the letters run across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-handed card game from 17th-century Spain.

clue.text: Irritating one about cutting an item

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: cutting means the abbreviation for about slices into the word for item

parts.note: a thing is an item
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone annoying is wondering about slicing a product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives C, from circa, which 'cutting' places inside THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing a tingling urge to scratch, so annoying or irritating.

clue.text: Pecked at, a writer lost some blood

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
to lose blood is to bleed, past tense bled

explanation.surface: A pen-pusher was attacked by birds and bled a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'writer' is the pen's point, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Took small bites at something, as a bird does with its beak.

clue.text: Firm producing spun threads

indicators.note: spun means turned around and twisted, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A business making yarn from fibres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' rearranges THREADS; 'Firm' is an adjective, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidly hardened or fixed in place, so firm.

clue.text: Theatre worker respecting craft in the German male

indicators.note: in places these short pieces within the German article

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
re means respecting or concerning
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A stagehand concerned with a boat is inside a German man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German male' is DER, the masculine German article, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre assistant who helps actors with their costumes between scenes.
